analysis.title: Mangroves and seawalls: household choices in Semarang
analysis.raw_text: Semarang is sinking faster than the sea is rising. This study asks how households choose between hard defences and restored mangroves, and what each choice costs them. Households near restored mangroves reported less flood damage, and their willingness to pay for protection grew once they had seen the mangroves work. We surveyed 412 households in six coastal neighbourhoods between March and June 2021, and interviewed 24 residents, village officials and fishing groups. Flood damage was recorded for the 2020 and 2021 seasons and compared by distance to the seawall and to restored mangrove belts. We surveyed 412 households in six coastal neighbourhoods between March and June 2021. Households living within 500 metres of restored mangrove cover reported 38 percent less flood damage than those behind the seawall. Flood exposure was highest in the northern kampungs, where land subsidence exceeds eight centimetres a year. Land subsidence, driven by groundwater extraction, doubled the area flooded by ordinary spring tides between 2010 and 2020. Residents valued the seawall for the certainty it gave, but most expected it to need raising again within fifteen years. Risk perception fell sharply among families who had lived behind the seawall for more than a decade. Willingness to pay for mangrove protection rose when households had seen restored belts reduce wave height. Community participation in replanting was strongest where fishing groups kept the right to harvest shellfish. Mangroves and seawalls are not alternatives but partners: the wall buys time while the mangroves grow. Protection that households can see working earns their support, and their money.

thread.title: Do mangroves or seawalls reduce flood damage more?

messages.content: Do mangroves or seawalls reduce flood damage more?

Across the papers in this repository, **restored mangroves reduced flood damage more than seawalls where there was room for them**, but the studies treat the two as complements rather than rivals.

- In Semarang, households near restored mangrove belts reported about 38 percent less flood damage than those behind the seawall (Mangroves and seawalls: household choices in Semarang, 2022).
- Seawalls gave the most certain protection in dense districts with no space for planting, at a higher maintenance cost (Nature-based coastal defence: a study of Bangkok, 2022).
- Where land is sinking, both lose protection over time unless groundwater extraction is controlled (Rethinking coastal land subsidence in Colombo, 2013); one study argues the wall mainly buys time while mangroves establish (Measuring community-based mangrove management across Mani…, 2024).

The evidence is strongest for mangroves in low-wave, muddy coasts; the papers disagree about exposed, high-energy shorelines.
